_meta.indication: DANYELZA is indicated, in combination with GM-CSF, for the treatment of pediatric patients 1 year of age and older and adult patients with relapsed or refractory high-risk neuroblastoma in the bone or bone marrow who have demonstrated a partial response, minor response, or stable disease to prior therapy.

pivotal_trials.population: Patients 1 year of age and older with relapsed or refractory high-risk neuroblastoma with primary refractory disease or incomplete response to salvage treatment in the bone or bone marrow
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR) by blinded independent review per revised INRC
pivotal_trials.result: Confirmed ORR 34% (95% CI 20%, 51%); 10 complete responses (26%) and 3 partial responses (8%); 23% of the 13 responders had observed DOR of 6 months

pivotal_trials.population: High-risk neuroblastoma with primary refractory or incomplete response to salvage treatment in bone and/or bone marrow
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR) by independent review per INRC
pivotal_trials.result: Confirmed ORR 45% (95% CI 24%, 68%); 30% of the 10 responders had observed DOR of at least 6 months

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥25%) include infusion-related reaction, pain, tachycardia, vomiting, cough, nausea, diarrhea, decreased appetite, hypertension, fatigue, peripheral neuropathy, and pyrexia. Serious infusion-related reactions occurred in 4% of patients in Study 201 and 18% in Study 12-230.
target_moa: Humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody directed against the glycolipid disialoganglioside GD2, which is widely expressed on neuroectoderm-derived tumors; established pharmacologic class is GD2-binding monoclonal antibody, mediating cytotoxicity including ADCC.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: SERIOUS INFUSION-RELATED REACTIONS and NEUROTOXICITY — DANYELZA can cause serious infusion reactions (including cardiac arrest, anaphylaxis, hypotension, bronchospasm, stridor) and severe neurotoxicity (including severe neuropathic pain, transverse myelitis, and RPLS).

rems.type: In the opinion of the review team, a REMS was not necessary for the proposed application; a boxed warning was included instead.

advisory_committee.vote: The Division did not refer this BLA to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee (ODAC).

surrogate_endpoint.text: Overall response rate (ORR), defined as the sum of partial and complete responses, supported by duration of response (DoR).

citations.quote: The BLA is submitted for Accelerated Approval based on the surrogate endpoint of overall response rate (ORR), defined as the sum of partial (PR) and complete responses (CR), supported by duration of response (DoR), which is defined as the interval between first response and progressive disease.

confirmatory_requirement.text: Submit the final report from an ongoing multicenter clinical trial to verify and further characterize the clinical benefit of naxitamab, enrolling a minimum of 80 patients (PMR 3950-1).

citations.quote: **3950-1** Submit the final report, including datasets, from an ongoing multicenter clinical trial to verify and further characterize the clinical benefit of naxitamab for the treatment of patients with relapsed or refractory neuroblastoma in combination with granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) in bone or bone marrow who have demonstrated a partial response, minor response, or stable disease to prior therapy

Enroll a minimum of 80 patients with evaluable disease and systematically follow all responding patients for at least 12 months from the onset of response, or until disease progression, whichever comes first.

orphan_indication.text: Naxitamab for the treatment of neuroblastoma has orphan drug status.

citations.quote: In addition, naxitamab for the treatment of neuroblastoma has orphan drug status; therefore, naxitamab is exempt from the requirements of PREA.

basis.text: The application was reviewed under Priority review.

summary.text: DANYELZA received Accelerated Approval based on the surrogate endpoint of ORR supported by DoR from two single-arm, open-label trials, under Priority review, with a post-marketing confirmatory trial required to verify clinical benefit. Naxitamab held orphan drug status and a Rare Pediatric Disease Designation for neuroblastoma.

citations.quote: In the opinion of the review team, the submitted evidence meets the statutory evidentiary standard for accelerated approval. The recommendation for accelerated approval is based on the results from two single-arm, open-label trials: Trial 201 (NCT 03363373) and Trial 12-230 (NCT 01757626).
Priority or Standard	Priority

Naxitamab for the treatment of neuroblastoma was granted a Rare Pediatric Disease Designation by FDA. In addition, naxitamab for the treatment of neuroblastoma has orphan drug status; therefore, naxitamab is exempt from the requirements of PREA.

requirement.text: 3950-1: Submit the final report from an ongoing multicenter clinical trial to verify and further characterize the clinical benefit of naxitamab in combination with GM-CSF; enroll a minimum of 80 patients with evaluable disease and follow responders for at least 12 months.

citations.quote: **3950-1** Submit the final report, including datasets, from an ongoing multicenter clinical trial to verify and further characterize the clinical benefit of naxitamab for the treatment of patients with relapsed or refractory neuroblastoma in combination with granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) in bone or bone marrow who have demonstrated a partial response, minor response, or stable disease to prior therapy; and to provide a more precise estimation of overall response rate and duration of response (according to the revised International Neuroblastoma Response Criteria by blinded independent review). Enroll a minimum of 80 patients with evaluable disease and systematically follow all responding patients for at least 12 months from the onset of response, or until disease progression, whichever comes first.

requirement.text: 3950-2: Conduct a comprehensive analysis characterizing the incidence, clinical presentation, management, and outcome of naxitamab-associated infusion-related reactions.

citations.quote: **3950-2** Conduct a comprehensive analysis evaluating and characterizing the incidence, clinical presentation, management, and outcome of the potential serious risk of naxitamab-associated infusion-related reactions in a sufficient number of patients to adequately characterize the risk.

requirement.text: 3950-3: Conduct a repeat-dose juvenile animal toxicology study in a pharmacologically relevant species to measure toxicity, particularly effects on the central and peripheral nervous system.
